question: [PRACTICE] What will the average "new forecasters per day" be on this question before this question closes?

calls.reasoning: Resolution is (forecasters shown in the Metaculus UI at close) / (days open). Denominator: the open date is not public (Metaculus returns 403 unauthenticated), but post-ID adjacency (44877 = Jul-27 MiniBench wave, ~45306-45366 = Aug-24 wave, 45534/45544 = Sep-7 wave, ~14/day site-wide) puts post 45516 at ~Sep 5-6, and a dated API pull recorded the Fall slug as absent from the projects API on 2026-09-03; so ~22-23 days, close 2026-09-28T05:59Z. Numerator: the reference class is prior-season warm-up questions that close at their season start - the Summer 2026 analog closed with 156 forecasters, which over this question's window is ~6.9/day, my anchor. I shade to ~110 forecasters (~4.9/day) for two reasons: the Summer practice batch shows a by-type spread (binary 180 vs discrete 80 in the testing area) and this is discrete, and accrual so far is slow (the same-titled testing-area twin showed 14 forecasters ~4 days in, Sep 9). Pulling up: the field grew to 267 Summer entrants, live MiniBench questions draw 140-160 forecasters each with little binary/numeric gap (159 vs 140), and warm-up traffic is back-loaded into the final week before a season start - most of the eventual count is still ahead of Now. No human market prices this (searched Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold, bookmakers; none found, and none would match the instrument). Escapes: 4% above 10.05 needs ~225+ forecasters, i.e. a Fall field far above Summer's binary warm-up; 2% below 0.95 needs under ~22 forecasters total, which the twin's early accrual already argues against.

No human market exists on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi. 15% above the 10.05 bound needs ~230+ forecasters on a 22-day window, which one more week at the current arrival pace would deliver; no mechanism exists below 0.95 (it would need a 125-day window).
